candidate.answerReason: Jane walks twice as fast as Hector, so Hector covers one third of the 18-block perimeter before their first meeting. Walking 6 blocks in Hector's indicated direction takes him exactly to D.

methods.label: Divide the perimeter by their walking rates
methods.explanation:
Jane takes half as much time to walk the same distance, so she walks twice as fast as Hector. During their shared walking time, Jane therefore covers twice Hector's distance.

[Figure 1](figures/1995_AMC_8_Q11_question_fig1.svg)

The grid is 6 blocks wide and 3 blocks tall, so the outside route has length
\[
2(6+3)=18\text{ blocks}.
\]
Because they start together and walk in opposite directions, their distances add to one full perimeter at their first meeting. Their distances are in the ratio \(2:1\), so Hector walks one of three equal shares:
\[
18\div 3=6\text{ blocks}.
\]
From the indicated start, Hector walks 3 blocks right to \(E\), then 3 blocks up to \(D\). Thus they meet exactly at \(D\), and the answer is \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
